output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Analysts did confirm 37 cases in September and 36 in October, in line with the earlier ~38 a month. Brackwater's analyst jump host runs a script that checks every ~5 minutes for confirmed incidents carrying the SLA warning. It then changes the category of each one to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" about 3.5 hours after opening. It did this to 47 cases, all through the integration account that was given category-edit rights at migration. Those cases drop out of the incident count and the containment-time and SLA figures. That is why the count falls, why containment looks like 100%, and why the monitoring queue has grown. This looks deliberate, though I haven't established who wrote the script or why. A connector fault is ruled out, since the connector itself never wrote a category. Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the 60k bonus. Next: restore the 47 cases, have the in-house team and Halvard check whether each was actually contained (only 11 notes mention containment), remove category-edit rights from the integration role, and get Brackwater's written explanation before renewal. Hold off on service-credit claims until the contract wording is checked. I haven't tested whether the 28 dropped detection rules left gaps. Review that separately.
